proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, 3^n is congruent to 3^(n mod 6) modulo 7.

argument.text: At n = 0 both sides equal 1 modulo 7.
The residue 3 has order 6 modulo 7: for every n in [0, 54], 3^(n+6) is congruent to 3^n modulo 7.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, n^3 is congruent to n modulo 6.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
There exists an integer n in [1, 60] with n^2 > 60.
Every n in [0, 60] falls in exactly one residue class modulo 6.
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 60].
Periodicity plus the base case gives the statement for every n in [0, 60].
